title: Fairness in Graph Mining: A Survey
venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
abstract: Graph mining algorithms have been playing a significant role in myriad fields over the years. However, despite their promising performance on various graph analytical tasks, most of these algorithms lack fairness considerations. As a consequence, they could lead to discrimination towards certain populations when exploited in human-centered applications. Recently, algorithmic fairness has been extensively studied in graph-based applications. In contrast to algorithmic fairness on independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) data, fairness in graph mining has exclusive backgrounds, taxonomies, and fulfilling techniques. In this survey, we provide a comprehensive and up-to-date introduction of existing literature under the context of fair graph mining. Specifically, we propose a novel taxonomy of fairness notions on graphs, which sheds light on their connections and differences. We further present an organized summary of existing techniques that promote fairness in graph mining. Finally, we discuss current research challenges and open questions, aiming at encouraging cross-breeding ideas and further advances.

claims.text: Traditional algorithmic fairness notions designed for i.i.d. data cannot capture the bias exhibited by graph relational topology.
Information propagation mechanisms in Graph Neural Networks induce bias in output node embeddings when performed on a biased graph topology.
Fairness notions in graph mining can be categorized into group fairness, individual fairness, counterfactual fairness, degree-related fairness, and application-specific fairness.

Techniques for promoting fairness in graph mining can be categorized into optimization with regularization, optimization with constraint(s), rebalancing, adversarial learning, edge rewiring, and orthogonal projection.

limitations.text: The surveyed fairness notions are by no means complete, as other types of biases could also exist depending on the needs of different real-world scenarios.
Most existing related survey papers are under the context of i.i.d. data or limited to either a certain application scenario or a certain type of graph mining algorithm.
Orthogonal projection only guarantees that embeddings and sensitive features are uncorrelated, while excluding non-linear dependency remains under-explored.

future_work.text: Designing new fairness notions or choosing sets of non-conflicting fairness notions tailored for specific graph mining algorithms and downstream applications.
Promoting multiple types of fairness simultaneously without causing conflicts or degrading overall model performance on graphs.
Achieving Pareto optimality in the trade-off between model utility and algorithmic fairness in graph mining.
Systematically explaining how unfairness arises from the interaction between graph topology and specific graph mining algorithm mechanisms.
Enhancing the robustness of algorithmic fairness in graph mining against biased supervision or adversarial manipulation.

methodologies.name: Taxonomy and systematic review of fair graph mining
methodologies.description: A comprehensive survey categorizing fairness notions into five groups and fairness-improving techniques into six categories across graph analytical tasks.
